Definition: {a termination (literally or figuratively); also (by implication) a portion; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after}
BiblicalUsage: The toes of the image are part iron and part clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly broken. And at the end of twelve months Nebuchadnezzar walks in his palace — the word is the portion and the termination, the end of a span.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe kingdoms are partly strong and partly broken, and Daniel saw that no empire is whole.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
